title: Iterated Narrow Networks: Turing Completeness at Width 4 on Convex Input Spaces and the Complexity of Verification
claim: A single iteration decomposes into a simulation stage and a certificate-accumulation stage that map input registers to updated registers.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, input registers to staged modules to output registers
description: A wide, flat diagram with three columns. On the left, four stacked boxes list the input registers: x1 left tape, x2 state concatenated with right tape, x3 scratch, and x4 certificate. In the middle are two rounded gray boxes. Stage 1 is labeled 'width-3 TM step inspired from Bournez et al. [2025]'. Stage 2+3 is labeled 'certificate' and gives the update x4' ← max{x4, ε(x1, x2)}. Solid arrows run from x1, x2 and x3 into Stage 1, and from Stage 1 to the primed outputs x1', x2' and x3'. Dashed gray arrows run from x1 and x2 into the certificate stage. A single arrow leads from the certificate stage to x4' certificate'. On the right, four stacked boxes list the primed output registers. The design is black and white with gray fill, and the eye goes first to the two bold stage boxes in the middle.
caption: One iteration of the width-4 network of Theorem 3: x1 holds the left tape, x2 co-encodes the state and the right tape, x3 is a scratch register, and x4 accumulates the certificate ε via the max update, with ε(x1, x2) = 0 iff the leading digits and the state prefix are valid (Remark 33).
abstract: We study the iterates of a fixed ReLU network $N$ of width 4, that is, the discrete-time system $x_{k+1} = N(x_k)$ on $[0,1]^4$. Equivalently, $x_k$ is the output of a weight-tied network made of $k$ copies of $N$, or of a recurrent network with no external input, started at $x_0$. We prove that every deterministic Turing machine $M$ admits such a network $N_M$. The network can be constructed in polynomial time from $M$. Each iteration has depth $\mathrm{poly}(|M|)$. The iterates of $N_M$ simulate $M$ exactly on every encoded tape. The number of iterations is proportional to the running time of $M$. Moreover, the fourth coordinate irreversibly flags every point of the convex cube $[0,1]^4$ whose simulation reads an invalid digit. This flag is the certificate that makes hardness reductions sound on convex input regions, the regime of practical verifiers. Convex regions were previously inaccessible because of a continuity obstruction inherent to ReLU networks. The correspondence has three consequences. First, reachability for iterated width-4 ReLU networks spans the full complexity hierarchy along the single axis of the time bound: it is NP-complete for a unary bound, NEXP-complete for a binary bound and RE-complete (undecidable) with no bound. Second, two extra neurons of width suffice to extend the hardness to every common smooth activation: at width 6, the robust verification problem (a promise problem with $Î´/2Î´$ gap) is NP-complete for $\tanh$, sigmoid, GELU, Swish, ELU, and any polynomial-time-computable continuous non-polynomial activation with a polynomial-time-computable Lipschitz constant. Third, the whole spectrum transfers to discretized Neural ODEs in dimension 5.
